exclusion_detail: Lead 8g (indol-3-ylmethylene hydrazinyl thiazole) needs the substituted hydrazinecarbothioamide 6g, whose preparation is never described, and the printed 'general procedure' for the final cyclocondensation step is a copy of the 2a/2b acetone/K2CO3 text, so the actual conditions for 8g are not given (only Table 1 optimisation: EtOH/H2O 1:1, microwave 70 C, 10 min). Counting 6g's preparation the route would also be 5 reactions (sesamol to 2a, 4a, 5a, 6g, 8g).

lead.label: 8g
lead.why: Abstract: 'Compound 8g and 8h were displayed remarkable antiproliferative activity ... Compound 8g showed higher potency as a cytotoxic molecule then fluorouracil' (8g is called 'the most potent compound' in the Biology section).

notes: Paper has no SI in the bundle. Intermediates 2a (formylation of sesamol with paraformaldehyde/MgCl2/Et3N), 4a (chloroacetone, K2CO3, acetone) and 5a (Br2, CHCl3) have procedures, but every final compound depends on the unprepared thiosemicarbazones 6a-j (none described, not stated commercial). The paper also names the thiazole attachment inconsistently (4-yl in the text/scheme description, 5-yl in the spectral headings). Procedure text for 5a lists the yield/purification as '2a and 2b' (copy error). Other compounds share the same missing 6x preparation, so none qualifies.
